strengths: Well-motivated research question addressing genuine gap in LLM development: pretraining hyperparameters optimized for validation loss without considering downstream adaptability
Comprehensive experimental design spanning multiple model families (Llama-2, OLMo-2), sizes (0.5B-4B), training regimes (20/140 TPP), and six CoT tasks with six evaluation metrics
Counterintuitive and important empirical finding: models with higher pretraining validation loss can outperform lower-loss models after fine-tuning (e.g., OLMo-2-1B-140x example)
Multi-faceted mechanistic analysis through linear probing (representation separability), pseudo-rank computation (attention regularization), and train-val gap (overfitting reduction)
Clear presentation with well-organized sections, informative figures, extensive appendices with training hyperparameters, and honest discussion of limitations
Consistent findings across multiple model families and sizes strengthen generalizability within tested scope
weaknesses: Severe scale limitations: models capped at 4B parameters while modern LLMs operate at 7B-405B; authors acknowledge but provide no evidence findings generalize to larger scales, severely limiting practical relevance

Limited task diversity: all six downstream tasks are Chain-of-Thought reasoning (math/medical/biomedical/knowledge/reading); no instruction-following, generation, or retrieval tasks; only zero-shot evaluation

Mechanistic analysis lacks causality: Section 5 demonstrates correlation not causation; no ablation studies to establish that proposed mechanisms actually drive plasticity improvements; interactions between mechanisms unexplored

Unclear practical applicability: optimal weight decay varies across regimes (1.0 for 20 TPP vs. 0.3 for 140 TPP); no guidance for practitioners when pretraining and downstream objectives conflict; trade-offs insufficiently explored

Statistical rigor gaps: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests on main results; single runs per configuration; Pearson correlations (Figure 3) show high variance with unstable LOO analysis (Figure 9)

Fine-tuning hyperparameters fixed across weight decay variants without justification: may prevent convergence for some configurations; only 3 epochs without convergence analysis; outcome reward model used for evaluation but not validated against human preferences

Incomplete analysis of regime dependence: optimal weight decay reverses at 140 TPP (favoring 0.1) vs. 20 TPP (favoring 1.0), attributed to learning rate schedule differences but not thoroughly investigated
Reproducibility concerns: code availability not mentioned; training on proprietary datasets; external reward model introduces potential bias; no mention of random seeds or multiplicity of runs
Linear probe methodology: probing hyperparameters not tuned per weight decay value; indirect measure that doesn't prove fine-tuning leverages linear separability
Limited scope of mechanistic analysis: only attention matrices examined; layer normalization, residuals, and interactions with other hyperparameters not analyzed

strengths: Comprehensive and systematic experimental design spanning multiple model families (Llama-2, OLMo-2), sizes (0.5B-4B), training regimes (20/140 TPP), and diverse downstream tasks (12 tasks across CoT reasoning, language understanding, and safety)

Consistent and robust findings across different experimental conditions, with extensive hyperparameter sweeps in appendices showing weight decay's effect holds across pretraining/fine-tuning variations
Important practical insight that optimal weight decay differs between pretraining and downstream objectives, challenging current practice of optimizing solely on pretraining loss
End-to-end perspective aligned with actual model development pipeline (pretraining → fine-tuning), making findings practically relevant

Provides mechanistic insights across three dimensions (linear representation separability, attention rank reduction, reduced overfitting) with strong correlations (e.g., r=0.87 for probing-downstream performance)
Honest and transparent discussion of limitations (correlational mechanisms, small samples for large models, scope constraints) with appropriate caveats on claims
weaknesses: Mechanistic explanations are correlational rather than causal—no ablation studies isolate whether linear separability or attention rank reduction causally drives improved plasticity, or whether both are side effects of the same mechanism
Limited scope reduces generalization confidence: experiments restricted to models ≤4B parameters; unclear if findings hold at 7B+ scale where different phenomena may emerge
Fine-tuning evaluation limited to supervised fine-tuning only (3 epochs); unclear if findings generalize to modern post-training (RLHF, DPO) or longer adaptation horizons

Practical guidance is model-specific without a priori selection mechanism—optimal weight decay varies (0.3-1.0 depending on model/regime), requiring expensive pre-training sweeps for each new configuration

Analysis of pretraining-downstream decoupling (Section 4.3) somewhat overstated: Figure 3/9 show generally negative correlations with high variability, and Figure 10 stability analysis reveals leave-one-out correlations are unstable
Small sample sizes acknowledged for largest models (Llama-2-4B-20x, OLMo-2-1B-140x) limit confidence in extrapolation; safety alignment task evaluation is minimal (single dataset)

Missing ablations and comparisons: no empirical comparison with other regularization approaches (dropout, label smoothing) that might also improve plasticity; no ablation quantifying relative importance of three proposed mechanisms
